wimera.t: Industrial IoT RAG Assistant — Wimera Systems
wimera.s: Full Stack Intern · Apr–Oct 2025 · Bengaluru · Python, FastAPI, RAG
b:
The Context

Wimera builds monitoring systems for factories. Machines stream telemetry around the clock; the resulting logs are voluminous, noisy, and only readable by people who know the schemas. My internship problem: make that data answerable in plain English for production engineers.

System Architecture

Machine telemetry ──▸ Ingestion & cleaning │ ▼ Chunking + embeddings ──▸ Vector index │ Engineer question ──▸ Retrieval ◂───────┘ │ ▼ Grounded LLM answer ──▸ Dashboard / report

A retrieval-augmented pipeline over the IoT data: logs are processed, chunked, and embedded; questions retrieve the relevant slices; the LLM answers grounded in what was retrieved rather than from memory.

What I Built

  • The RAG chatbot — end to end: ingestion, chunking strategy for time-series log data, retrieval, and grounded generation.
  • Automated reporting pipeline — converts raw IoT logs into human-readable summaries on a schedule, removing a manual analysis step.
  • Dashboard integration — AI-generated insights surfaced inside the monitoring dashboards teams already used, instead of yet another tool.
  • Multi-tenant access controls — hard organization-level isolation, so each client only ever queries its own machines' data.

What It Taught Me

Production RAG is 20% model, 80% data discipline: chunking decisions, retrieval quality, and grounding matter more than prompt cleverness. And the multi-tenant work taught me that security design is backend engineering, not an afterthought.

urlshort.s: Python · FastAPI · PostgreSQL · Redis · Docker · Nginx · AWS EC2
b:
Overview

A deliberately simple product built the hard way: the goal was to learn what it takes to keep a read-heavy service fast under load — the same shape as any high-traffic redirect, CDN edge, or feature-flag lookup.

Architecture

Client ──▸ Nginx (reverse proxy / LB) │ ┌───────┴───────┐ ▼ ▼ FastAPI ×N FastAPI ×N (horizontally scalable) │ │ ▼ ▼ Redis ◂── hot path (cache) │ miss ▼ PostgreSQL ◂── source of truth ▲ background workers — click analytics

Key Decisions

  • Cache-first redirects: the redirect path never touches Postgres if Redis can answer — that's what holds <10ms p99.
  • Async everywhere: FastAPI with connection pooling; analytics writes go through background workers so a click count never blocks a redirect.
  • Stateless app tier: instances scale horizontally behind Nginx because all state lives in Redis/Postgres.
  • Managed data stores: traded some control for reliability and easier ops.

Challenges

The interesting problems were cache invalidation on updated links, keeping analytics eventually-consistent without losing clicks, and tuning pool sizes so bursts didn't exhaust connections.

Results

<10ms p99 redirect latency under read-heavy load, with the database shielded by the cache layer. Full setup and decisions documented in the repo.

convai.s: Python · FastAPI · FasterWhisper · KokoroTTS · Docker · LM Studio
b:
Overview

Talk to an LLM out loud and have it talk back — with latency low enough that it feels like conversation, not dictation. Every stage runs locally.

Architecture

Mic audio ──▸ FasterWhisper (STT) │ text ▼ LLM via LM Studio ◂── conversation context │ reply ▼ KokoroTTS (voice) │ audio ▼ Speaker

A FastAPI backend orchestrates the loop: capture, transcription, generation, synthesis — with conversation context carried across turns.

Key Decisions

  • FasterWhisper over vanilla Whisper for transcription speed — the loop lives or dies on STT latency.
  • Streaming-minded pipeline: each stage starts as early as possible instead of waiting for the previous one to fully finish.
  • Local inference via LM Studio: private, free to run, and great for iterating.
  • Single Docker container so the whole stack ships as one unit.

Challenges

Latency budgeting across three models in a row, and keeping the conversation context useful without letting it bloat generation time.

Results

Bidirectional voice conversation with context carried across turns, responsive enough to interrupt and redirect — a working foundation for voice-agent experiments.

localrag.s: Python · Flask · FAISS · SentenceTransformers · PyMuPDF · LM Studio
b:
Overview

RAG without the cloud: drop in your PDFs, ask questions, get grounded answers — and nothing ever leaves your machine. Built for anyone whose documents can't go to a third-party API.

Architecture

PDFs ──▸ PyMuPDF extract ──▸ Chunking │ ▼ SentenceTransformers embeddings │ ▼ FAISS index │ Question ──▸ embed ──▸ similarity search │ top-k chunks ▼ LM Studio LLM (offline) ──▸ grounded answer

Key Decisions

  • FAISS for vector search — fast, local, zero infrastructure.
  • Context-grounded prompting: the model answers from retrieved chunks and is pushed to say so when the documents don't contain the answer — the main defense against hallucination.
  • Flask APIs for ingestion, document management, and querying, so the system is usable programmatically, not just as a demo.

Challenges

Chunking strategy dominates answer quality — too small loses context, too large dilutes retrieval. Getting PDF extraction clean across messy real-world documents was its own fight.

Results

A fully offline, privacy-first document Q&A system — the architecture I later applied at production scale during the Wimera internship.

amazonml.s: Amazon ML Challenge ’26 · Team ZERO · LightGBM · TF-IDF · Modal · MIT
b:
Problem Statement

Given a deduplicated reference list (S1), locate every matching business record in two additional datasets (S2, S3). 24.2 million records processed in total — 1.73M S1 + 10.0M S2/S3 test records — spanning the US, India, and France.

Dataset Characteristics

Deliberately hostile: mixed scripts (nine Indic scripts in the Indian data), injected typos, planted look-alike records designed to fool matchers, and almost no postcodes to anchor on.

Stage 1 — Preprocessing & Normalization

Custom transliteration maps nine Indic scripts to Latin using a single offset table. A phonetic consonant skeleton then collapses spelling variants — 'global' and its Tamil rendering both reduce to klpl. Mojibake, honorifics, and formatting noise are stripped; canonical states extracted per country.

Stage 2 — Candidate Generation (Blocking)

Five TF-IDF nearest-neighbor searches, constrained by country and state blocks, generate candidate pairs — recovering 95.4% of true pairs from just 0.0004% of the possible pair space, capped at 20 candidates per S1 record per source.

Stage 3 — Matching Model

A LightGBM classifier scores pairs on 46 features spanning name, address, legal form, and competitive context. The decision threshold optimizes macro F0.5 per S1 record. Context features — how each candidate ranks among its competitors — drove 64% of model gains. Extracting legal form from raw text exposed planted look-alikes that normalization had masked.

Validation & Results

  • 0.949 macro F0.5 — public leaderboard
  • 0.961 held-out validation (0.981 precision / 0.916 recall)
  • ~2 hours end-to-end on 16 cores via Modal — pure Python, no external APIs or lookups

Figures above are public-leaderboard and internal-validation results; leaderboard top scores reached ~0.99. The repo documents unfinished experiments in reverse search and reranking.

Lessons Learned

Reading errors beat tuning models. Manually analyzing 25 misclassified examples produced the single largest score improvement (+0.019 to +0.021) — more than any hyperparameter sweep. MIT-licensed as a reproducible baseline.
